story.head: Something has to give
paras: The Devils (8-5-0) lost 5-2 to Colorado on Wednesday, while the Golden Knights (9-4-1) beat Ottawa 4-1 on Tuesday. Going in, the Devils are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (tied for fourth).

The Devils have played better than their record (.615) says: their chances are worth about .747, and their goaltending has held them back. The Golden Knights’ record (.679) is about what their chances are worth.

The Devils keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and block more shots than almost anyone (3rd). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Devils’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. The Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Jack Hughes (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Devils in scoring, and Nico Hischier (7 G / 2 A / 9 P in 13 GP) has a team-high seven goals. Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 14 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Mark Stone (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Connor Hellebuyck (1-0-0 / .944 SV% in 1 GS) is expected to start for New Jersey, and Adin Hill (5-1-0 / .895 SV% in 6 GS) for Vegas.
At home, Ryan Craig likes to send Connelly, Hertl and Bowman out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Lombardi, Glass and Brown.

Brayden McNabb is set to play his 900th NHL game.
Jack Hughes has three goals on chances worth about 6.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Mitch Marner has a point in eight straight games.
